Q: how to query on many to one mapping with jpa repository A:

Correct your query like this:

select distinct 
    n.adapterInstance 
from 
    NodeAdapterInstanceDetails n 
    join n.adapterKindDetails ad
    join ad.nodeDetails nd
where 
    nd.clientName = :client_name

select 
    n 
from 
    NodeAdapterInstanceDetails n 
    join n.adapterKindDetails ad
    join ad.nodeDetails nd
where 
    n.adapterInstance = :adapter_instance and 
    nd.clientName = :client_name

To get ability to use the linked entity filed you first have to 'join' this entity.

More info: JPQL Language Reference

Q: Convert RGB values to equivalent HSV values using Python A:

Based on array indexing and slicing in NumPy, this is my approach for the forward:

import numpy as np

def rgb2hsv(rgb):
    """ Convert RGB to HSV color space

    :param rgb: np.ndarray
    :return: np.ndarray
    """

    rgb = rgb.astype('float')
    maxv = np.amax(rgb, axis=2)
    maxc = np.argmax(rgb, axis=2)
    minv = np.amin(rgb, axis=2)
    minc = np.argmin(rgb, axis=2)

    hsv = np.zeros(rgb.shape, dtype='float')
    hsv[maxc == minc, 0] = np.zeros(hsv[maxc == minc, 0].shape)
    hsv[maxc == 0, 0] = (((rgb[..., 1] - rgb[..., 2]) * 60.0 / (maxv - minv + np.spacing(1))) % 360.0)[maxc == 0]
    hsv[maxc == 1, 0] = (((rgb[..., 2] - rgb[..., 0]) * 60.0 / (maxv - minv + np.spacing(1))) + 120.0)[maxc == 1]
    hsv[maxc == 2, 0] = (((rgb[..., 0] - rgb[..., 1]) * 60.0 / (maxv - minv + np.spacing(1))) + 240.0)[maxc == 2]
    hsv[maxv == 0, 1] = np.zeros(hsv[maxv == 0, 1].shape)
    hsv[maxv != 0, 1] = (1 - minv / (maxv + np.spacing(1)))[maxv != 0]
    hsv[..., 2] = maxv

    return hsv

And backward color space conversion:

def hsv2rgb(hsv):
    """ convert HSV to RGB color space

    :param hsv: np.ndarray
    :return: np.ndarray
    """

    hi = np.floor(hsv[..., 0] / 60.0) % 6
    hi = hi.astype('uint8')
    v = hsv[..., 2].astype('float')
    f = (hsv[..., 0] / 60.0) - np.floor(hsv[..., 0] / 60.0)
    p = v * (1.0 - hsv[..., 1])
    q = v * (1.0 - (f * hsv[..., 1]))
    t = v * (1.0 - ((1.0 - f) * hsv[..., 1]))

    rgb = np.zeros(hsv.shape)
    rgb[hi == 0, :] = np.dstack((v, t, p))[hi == 0, :]
    rgb[hi == 1, :] = np.dstack((q, v, p))[hi == 1, :]
    rgb[hi == 2, :] = np.dstack((p, v, t))[hi == 2, :]
    rgb[hi == 3, :] = np.dstack((p, q, v))[hi == 3, :]
    rgb[hi == 4, :] = np.dstack((t, p, v))[hi == 4, :]
    rgb[hi == 5, :] = np.dstack((v, p, q))[hi == 5, :]

    return rgb

I was motivated to write these lines as I wasn't convinced by a pixel-wise conversion due to the computational overload and also did not want to rely on another library such as OpenCV.

Feel free to suggest a modification to make this solution more elegant and generic.

Q: I have issues jumping to my kernel in my bootloader A:

All of those print, enable_a20, and rdisk subroutines get called from within the real address mode. None of them should linger beneath that [bits 32]. Put the lot in between:

jmp 0x08:protected_mode

print:
enable_a20:
rdisk:

[bits 32]

Make it count

cli
hlt
jmp $

The infinite loop jmp $ should better read jmp $-2 so that the cli and hlt instructions can re-execute. (cli doesn't need to be in the loop, and if you're using a loop around hlt you don't need cli at all, it's ok to let the BIOS handle keyboard interrupts like ctr+alt+del reboots. Unless switching to 32-bit mode broke interrupts, in which case you should cli before that so there isn't a window where an interrupt would crash.)

Make it a habit

cli
mov eax, 0x10
mov ds, eax
mov es, eax
mov ss, eax
mov fs, eax
mov gs, eax
mov ebp, 0x90000
mov esp, ebp

Even while under the protection of cli, it is a good habit to ALWAYS change SS and SP in tandem AND in this order (you did it all right at the start):

cli
mov ebp, 0x90000
mov ax, 0x10
mov ds, ax
mov es, ax
mov fs, ax
mov gs, ax
mov ss, ax       ; 1st
mov esp, ebp     ; 2nd

Magic number

xor ax, ax
mov es, ax
mov bx, 0x8000

What is the use of defining KERNEL equ 0x8000 if you're not using it in your program?
And why repeat setting up ES=0 that was done at the start?
So this becomes:

mov bx, KERNEL

Trust BIOS for drive number

mov dl, 0x80

There's not much that you get from BIOS when your bootloader begins, but the number for the BootDrive you do receive in the DL register. Use it instead of this hard-coded 0x80.

Don't trust the BIOS for any other initial conditions except linear address 7C00, though. See Michael Petch's general tips for bootloader development.

Q: Domain vs DTO on database entity relations A:

Each domain has its own domain logics!

It's not seen whether you need to use DDD. Just for the described aim you can do it as you did. But if you want to use different ORM for different queries, or separate Command domain and Query domain model for highly write-intensive access to DB, -- I would rather choose DDD(+CQRS) to separate these responsibilities. - Domain deal only with CommandHandler - Or just in general if you'd like to realize another logics for any query - you can separate query and command logics in order to use another model for query.

But just to do 3 queries and combine them into 1 DTO-response, can be done asynchronously and even in parallel (depending on DB) by any ORM (configured by keys) or simply with correct SQL.

Whether to separete read and write concerns - you should add some logics (EventSourcing or INotifyPropertyChanged interface) to update your DbContext for View - so, you can update your DbContext in background to your client automatically to save DbContext up-to-date.

So it all depends on your technical tasks for the purpose to decide what patterns to use in development process.

P.S. example where can use domain in CQRS-pattern - in Command-model, while using DTOs in Query-module

P.P.S. for more info Architecture for Flow
